originality.rationale: Four actual semantic published-finding corpus searches and three public web searches exposed near matches for the same cyclic median object in unweighted ell_p perturbation, adjacent-edge BV, and conventional median theory, but no exact complete-pair Gini modulus. Full mathematical RESULT texts were compared for both closest published records; Qiu full author-hosted paper, selected primary pages of Maragos/Schafer and Arias-Castro/Donoho, and Restrepo/Chacon abstract were materially assessed. The new norm has different invariance and sharp dimension dependence, requiring a nontrivial all-subsets Gini cut bound; nevertheless unindexed historic equivalence remains possible.
residual_risks: Restrepo and Chacon (1994) full text not materially inspected; accessible abstract is only a partial comparison.
Maragos and Schafer 44-page report and Arias-Castro and Donoho 36-page study were not exhaustively read, so no whole-document noncoverage is claimed.
Unindexed historical equivalence or a general cut-dominating theorem not retrieved by semantic searches remains possible.
Closely related selector techniques are known; the new value rests on the exact Gini cut bound and dimension-resolved coefficient, not on independent invention of the linearization trick.

value.rationale: The global complete-pair Gini seminorm is a natural pairwise dispersion measure distinct from ell_p and cycle-edge variation. A standard robust smoothing filter has a complete and dimension-dependent two-input stability classification, the first amplification at four sites, explicit singleton extremizers, and an unattained envelope 3. The cut-capacity step is substantive and not a mere textual substitution into published ell_p/BV conclusions; no general downstream theorem is needed for this operator invariant.
